contract.intent: THE GATE CARD NEVER PROMISES A RUN THE ENGINE REFUSES — found by the operator reading the live card: when a task's gate is SUBMITTED and its executability is BLOCKED (an open declared dependency), the card states the refusal and then contradicts itself two lines later — `next: decide it now — accepting grill lets the work start`, and the step's own `what` (`the contract gate — approving it lets the work start`). detail.readiness sits unread a few fields above both. 12/18's AC-3 says the gate wait and the executability render as SEPARATE facts 'so neither is ever mistranslated into the other' — and this sentence IS the mistranslation: it asserts the ENGINE's answer (the run starts) from the HUMAN's fact (a gate was submitted). The operator's rule: a task with a dependency should read `waiting on <the dependency>`, not an unlock claim. The decision itself stays the human's (12/17: the block is on EXECUTION, not on gate decisions) — so Accept/Reject stay available and the card says exactly what they do. READS ONLY: no new state, no new event, no new status word, no new write path, no new dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: THE CARD CONSULTS READINESS — ONCE: the `next:` line and the step's `what` line are derived from detail.readiness (12/18's ONE derivation; the page never re-derives), so a submitted gate whose readiness is BLOCKED can never print an unlock claim. Proof: rendering a card whose grill is submitted and whose dependency is open prints NO 'lets the work start' / 'lets it land', and names the wait instead.

THE WAIT IS NAMED, NOT DESCRIBED: in that state the card reads `waiting on` with the DERIVATION's own blocker string — `dependency open: <id> (<status>)` (12/17's wording, never a second phrasing) — so the operator sees WHAT is being waited on, by id and status.

THE DECISION STAYS THE HUMAN'S, AND SAYS WHAT IT DOES: Accept and Reject remain available while the run is refused (12/17: a gate decision is not work — the operator may need to reject, cancel or defer), and the wording says exactly that and no more: an accept settles the CONTRACT and does not start the work. The card never implies the accept is pointless, and never implies it runs the task.
NO REGRESSION ON THE READY CASE: a submitted gate with readiness READY still reads 'accepting it lets the work start' (entry) and the confirm/close wording (exit) — pinned by test, unchanged.

ONE WORDING, EVERY ROW: the CLI leg card's TASKS list carries the per-task verdict too (12/18's `execVerdict`, the same formatter `ann status` and the plan use) — today it is the one row left printing a bare status. The page and the CLI never say different things about the same task.

READS ONLY + VERIFIED: no new event type, no new status, no new write path, no new deps, minimal vanilla UI. Full suite green, npm run typecheck clean, ann check/verify clean, committed with evidence.
